steps.message: Discrete LOD on the compatibility soft-mesh path. AsteroidBelt.proc is 30000 proxies x 80 triangles of unshared, flat-shaded geometry -- the case that made the single indirect draw's vertex stage the whole frame on A10-class hardware. The two captures are an A/B on r.lod.baseThreshold: 0 pins every proxy to LOD0, 128 is the shipping default.

steps.comment: ERT_Compatibility; otherwise this measures the wrong path entirely.
Always passes; the report's `actual` is the LOD0 baseline frame rate this A/B exists to compare against.
Baseline: every proxy at full detail.
Selecting a level must not desynchronise expansion from the indirect draw args.
Frame rate at the shipping threshold.
LOD active. Compared against the baseline this should differ only in distant silhouette detail -- no holes, no missing rocks, no scrambled triangles.

The one that actually exercises the mechanism. At this threshold the default camera splits the belt roughly 3200/14500/8800/3500 across all four levels, so a single indirect draw carries proxies pointing at four different index ranges at once. A mistake in the cull->expand->vertex offset handoff shows up here as scrambled or missing triangles; at the shipping threshold the whole belt collapses to one level and would hide it.
